description:
Found while resolving bd:JMAP-ly0n.14 (jmap-chat-types property enums). The canonical jmap-mail-types/src/backend.rs has the SAME defect: all 8 property selector enums (MailboxProperty, ThreadProperty, EmailProperty, IdentityProperty, EmailSubmissionProperty, VacationResponseProperty, SearchSnippetProperty, SieveScriptProperty) lack #[non_exhaustive].

This is the workspace canonical for the extension-types family per workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' table. The 6 newer siblings (calendars-types, tasks-types, contacts-types, filenode-types, sharing-types, metadata-types) all have #[non_exhaustive] on their property enums. The two oldest (jmap-mail-types canonical, jmap-chat-types) predate the convention.

Workspace AGENTS.md propagation rule: 'When you change the canonical, propagate the change to every sibling in the same pass'. Since chat-types was fixed in bd:JMAP-ly0n.14 ahead of the canonical, this bead fills the propagation gap.

Scope: add #[non_exhaustive] above each of the 8 pub enum declarations in crate-jmap-mail-types/src/backend.rs. One-line per enum. No behavior change, no wire-format change, attribute-order rule (#[non_exhaustive] -> #[derive] -> #[serde]) is satisfied.

Workspace AGENTS.md 'Canonical Templates' table calls jmap-mail-types the canonical for the extension-types family. Compliance with #[non_exhaustive] on public enums is a workspace-wide rule (workspace AGENTS.md 'Conventions and Patterns', 'Extras-preservation policy', the per-crate 'Settled Design Constraints' tables). The canonical violating its own rule is a maintenance hazard.
title: Add #[non_exhaustive] to property selector enums in canonical jmap-mail-types::backend
